initialRequiredFindings.problem: Nothing tests the callback guard for a closed or exiting queue (OutputEventQueue.cs:120), yet file-flush-interval.md:11 says closed/faulted/exiting queues ignore callbacks as an implemented T01 behavior. Every mode closes admission and lets the worker exit before the clock advances again, so no callback ever arrives after closure. If the admissionClosed check were removed, the fixtures would still pass: RegisterFlushBoundary only checks workerExiting/workerFinished, and the worker would run one extra flush after Complete.
initialRequiredFindings.suggestedFix: In the idle modes, before Cleanup, take the queue admissionGate. Under it call runtime.CloseAdmission(), then clock.Advance(interval), then Require(queue.RegisteredFlushCount == 0). The worker can't exit while the gate is held, so this callback hits the closed guard with the timer still owned. Then await Completion and Require(writer.Flushes == 2). Report fires=3 and update FileIntervalExpectations.cs:19 and verify-file-interval.py:32 to match.

initialRequiredFindings.problem: In the below/above modes the console level is None, so AcquireConsoleWriter never calls the acquirer and selections==0 is true regardless of order. The C# check (line 93), the native 'before acquisition' tuple (verify-file-interval.py:20) and the 'range' corruption control (line 68) therefore cannot detect a range check that runs after console acquisition. The production order (CoreLogRuntime.cs:93-103) is correct; only the evidence is missing.
initialRequiredFindings.suggestedFix: Use CoreLogLevel.Information for ConsoleLevel when invalid is true too, e.g. `disabled || failure || invalid`. Then selections==0 and workers==0 together show that the range check runs before both console acquisition and worker launch.

resolutions.resolution: Three controlled idle modes fire the still-owned timer after admission closes while holding the queue gate. No control registers, and actual writer calls remain two flushes while timer fires are three.
Invalid-range modes enable console. Both actual acquisitions and launched workers remain zero; C# and native matchers assert the acquisition fact.
